chapter_name: Patra Lekhan: Aupcharik Aur Anaupcharik (Letter Writing: Formal and Informal)
learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will master the structure of perfect letters, whether you are complaining to the mayor or inviting your best friend to a party!

main_concepts.concept_title: ✉️ The Power of Patra (Why we write)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Even in the age of WhatsApp, letters hold power! A text message can't get your street fixed, but a formal letter to the municipality will. Letters are structured, respectful ways of communicating thoughts, requests, or emotions across distances.

Formal letters are written to Principals, Government Officials, Editors, or Shopkeepers. The tone is strictly business—polite and direct. The most important rule? It MUST have a 'Vishay' (Subject line) so the busy official knows immediately what the letter is about!

Informal letters are for family, friends, and relatives. The tone is relaxed, emotional, and chatty. You ask about their health, share your feelings, and send love. There is NO 'Vishay' (Subject) in these letters because you don't need a business reason to talk to your mom!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🏗️ The Anatomy of a Letter (The Format)
main_concepts.simple_explanation:
A modern letter (left-aligned) has specific parts: 
1. Preshak ka Pata (Sender's Address) & Date. 
2. Praptkarta (Receiver's details - only for Formal). 
3. Vishay (Subject - only for Formal). 
4. Sambodhan (Greeting - like 'Mahoday' or 'Priya Mitra'). 
5. Main Body. 
6. Closing (like 'Bhavdiya' or 'Tumhara Mitra').

Did you know that writing a formal email follows the exact same logic as an Aupcharik Patra? The 'Subject' box is your 'Vishay', and the main body follows the same respectful tone. Mastering letter writing makes you a master of professional emails too!

fun_activity.title: 👽 The 'Alien Pen-Pal' Letter
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you have an alien pen-pal living on Mars. Write a short Anaupcharik (Informal) letter in Hindi telling them about your favorite Earth food (like Samosa or Pizza) and asking them what they eat on Mars!

quick_recap: ⭐ Aupcharik (Formal) letters are for officials and require a strict format, including a Vishay (Subject).
⭐ Anaupcharik (Informal) letters are for friends/family and have a relaxed, emotional tone with no Subject.
⭐ Modern Hindi letter formats are fully left-aligned.
⭐ The tone of an Aupcharik letter must be polite, concise, and to the point.
⭐ Greetings change based on the letter type: 'Mahoday' (Sir) for formal, 'Priya' or 'Pujya' for informal.
